statement: For f:X→Y, the following are equivalent: every pullback along a local isomorphism Y'→Y belongs to W; every X/y is W-aspherical.

statement: A functor f:X→Y is W-aspherical if every X/y is W-aspherical, equivalently if it passes all local-isomorphism pullback tests.

statement: If f has a right adjoint r, the comma category X/y is isomorphic to X/r(y), and therefore has a terminal object; f is W-aspherical.
If f has a left adjoint, f is W-coaspherical.

statement: The generalized right adjoint g:Y→[X^op,Set] is g(y)(x)=Hom_Y(fx,y), and X/y is the category of elements of g(y).

statement: If f:X→Y and g:Y→Z are W-aspherical, then gf is W-aspherical; the dual assertion holds for coaspherical functors.

statement: If f and gf are W-aspherical, then g is W-aspherical; likewise for coaspherical functors.

statement: A local isomorphism p:S'→S is a functor for which S'/s'→S/p(s') is an isomorphism for every s'; equivalently, p is a discrete fibration.

statement: Local isomorphisms are stable under composition.

statement: If gf and g are local isomorphisms, then f is a local isomorphism.

statement: Every isomorphism of categories is a local isomorphism.

statement: Local isomorphisms are stable under arbitrary base change.

statement: Aspherical functors are stable under base change by local isomorphisms, and coaspherical functors by co-local isomorphisms.

statement: For a nontrivial category Y with initial object y0 and another object y, the base change of {y0}→Y along {y}→Y is ∅→e, so W-asphericity is not stable under arbitrary base change when ∅ is not W-aspherical.

statement: Aspherical functors should be preserved by smooth base change, and coaspherical functors by proper base change.

statement: An equivalence of categories is both W-aspherical and W-coaspherical.

statement: For f:X→Y, the following conditions are equivalent: each X_y→X/y is W-coaspherical; each x\backslash X→f(x)\backslash Y has W-aspherical strict fibres; over every [1]→Y the terminal fibre inclusion is W-coaspherical; all outgoing lift categories L_f(x,u) are W-aspherical.

statement: In the pullback over [1], the comma category from an object of the terminal fibre to that fibre inclusion has an initial object; the remaining comma categories are the outgoing lift categories.

statement: A functor is W-proper when it satisfies the equivalent conditions of Proposition 3.

statement: The inclusion X_y→X/y has a left adjoint iff each outgoing lift category has an initial object, equivalently iff each covariant functor z↦Hom_u(x,z) on X_y is representable by u_*x.

statement: A weakly Cat-fibred functor, and hence an ordinary fibration, is W-smooth.

statement: W-proper and W-smooth functors are stable under arbitrary base change.

statement: W-proper functors are stable under composition; the same holds for W-smooth functors.

statement: Every co-local isomorphism is W-proper, so is every isomorphism and every closed immersion (cosieve inclusion).

statement: Every local isomorphism is W-smooth; in particular, every open immersion (sieve inclusion) is smooth.

statement: If f and gf are W-proper, then g satisfies the proper lifting condition at each object of the strict image of f; the dual assertion holds for smoothness.

statement: If f:X→Y is W-proper, then x\backslash f:x\backslash X→f(x)\backslash Y is W-proper for every x.

statement: A proper or smooth functor with W-aspherical strict fibres is universally a W-equivalence.

statement: For a proper map with aspherical fibres, every base change is W-aspherical; a universal W-equivalence has aspherical strict fibres.

statement: A universal W-equivalence need not be W-proper or W-smooth.

statement: A universal W-equivalence is universally W-aspherical (and dually universally coaspherical).

statement: For prelisse X/S, every fibre comparison X_s→Φ_S(X)_s=s\X belongs to W, universally.
repair: This is the universal prelisse condition itself. The replacement is split fibred, hence smooth; the comparison transfers fibre-inclusion assertions by two-out-of-three.

statement: The pseudofibration hypothesis passes from X to Φ_S(X).
repair: By the dual Proposition 8, all comma transports s1\X→s0\X belong to W. These are precisely the split replacement's transports.

statement: Lemma: pullback of a family in Fib0 defines a contravariant functor from Hom(S′,S) to Fib0(S′).
gap_or_error: An arbitrary Grothendieck fibration gives pullback transport only up to chosen coherent isomorphisms unless split data are fixed.
repair: Use the already split Φ_S(X), or replace the original fibration by a split one as the parenthesis allows. Then F∘f^op is strict and natural transformations give strict Cartesian functors.

statement: In that lemma every natural transformation of indexing functors induces a W^d-map of pulled-back families.
repair: The induced component at t is F(α_t):F(g(t))→F(f(t)) in W. For split fibrations fibrewise and right-local weak equivalences agree.
notes: Membership in W on total categories additionally uses the full relative W(2), not merely the assertion W^d.

statement: The first displayed transport is F∘f→F∘g for α:f→g.
gap_or_error: Contravariance reverses this arrow; the component display immediately below has the correct direction.
repair: Read F∘g^op→F∘f^op. The printed direction is preserved as an edition slip.

statement: The classifying functor F itself is 'in W fibre by fibre'.
gap_or_error: W classifies functors between categories, not the displayed Cat-valued diagram F; the intended arrow is F*α.
repair: Read the induced natural transformation F*α, equivalently its Cartesian functor of Grothendieck constructions, as fibrewise in W.
notes: Notational slip, not a failure of the lemma.

statement: Corollary 1: localized pullback factors through the groupoid completion of Hom(S′,S)^op.
repair: The lemma sends every arrow to an isomorphism; apply the universal property of groupoid completion.

statement: Connected indexing functors give isomorphic pulled-back objects, generally noncanonically.
repair: Choose a path in the functor category and compose the induced isomorphisms. Different paths need not agree; the C2-action example in the commentary exhibits distinct automorphisms on π0.

statement: Allowing the coefficient to vary gives a functor from the groupoid completion of Hom(S′,S) to the category of pullback functors.
repair: The component transports are natural in the coefficient. Inverting the contravariant transports after localization permits the displayed covariant convention; it is not an additional variance error.

statement: Homotopic indexing functors induce naturally isomorphic restriction functors on HOT^lc_W.
repair: Compose the natural transport isomorphisms along a finite zigzag of natural transformations.

statement: Corollary 2: a categorical homotopy equivalence of bases induces an equivalence on locally constant coefficients.
repair: Restrict along a homotopy inverse. The two composite homotopies give inverse equivalences up to natural isomorphism.
references: Cisinski2009LocallyConstant (Theorem 1.3, a later stronger ordinary-homotopy version)

statement: These results should use at most full W(2) rather than W(2 bis).
repair: The explicit total-category argument does use full relative W(2); the lemma's fibrewise/right-local statement is separate. No general equivalence of the weak and full localizer axioms is asserted.

statement: For categorically contractible S, constant coefficients give an equivalence Hot_W→HOT^lc_W(S).
repair: Apply Corollary 2 to S→e; a chosen object provides a homotopy inverse.

statement: A locally constant family over contractible S is isomorphic after localization to a product Z×S.
repair: This follows from the constant-coefficient equivalence, but the isomorphism alone is insufficient for the desired W-zigzag inference.

statement: The inclusion Z×{s}→Z×S lies in W, indeed is a categorical homotopy equivalence.
repair: A contraction of S to t and its value at s join id_S to c_s. Multiply the finite natural-transformation zigzag by Z.
notes: No product-closure theorem beyond preservation of categorical homotopies is needed.

statement: A W^d-map between smooth locally constant families preserves the property that fibre inclusion is in W.
repair: It is fibrewise in W; full W(2) gives a W-map on total categories. Two-out-of-three in the fibre-inclusion square gives the assertion.
notes: The source explicitly flags use of W(2), not merely W(2 bis).

statement: An abstract isomorphism in the localization does not by itself provide a chain consisting of the specified W^d-arrows.
repair: The objection is logically correct without a calculus or saturation argument. The source then constructs the needed actual maps from a chosen base homotopy.

statement: The homotopy id_S~fg supplies a finite chain of pulled-back split families joined by W^d=W^f maps.
repair: Write the actual sequence φ_j and apply contravariant transport at each step; relative W(2) makes the total comparison maps lie in W. Full proof in the finite-zigzag block.

statement: Proposition 9: a left W-fibration satisfies the hot-strong test on maps between categorically contractible bases.
gap_or_error: The footnotes reserve strong saturation for the localization-based inference and state that only an isomorphism in Hot_W has yet been obtained.
repair: The explicit finite contraction proof supplies actual W-maps and proves this contractible-base assertion under W(1,2,3), without strong saturation.

statement: The stronger complement: pullback of an arbitrary categorical homotopy equivalence along the family is a W-map.
gap_or_error: The following Hom calculation proves invertibility in Hot_W; membership in W requires strong saturation for that argument.
repair: Theorem 3(d) records the exact localized result. For full modern fundamental localizers W(2), Cisinski's strong-saturation theorem completes the inference.
notes: No extension of 4.2.4 to arbitrary weak fundamental localizers is claimed.

statement: For a universally prelisse family, literal pullback computes the derived restriction on locally constant coefficients.
repair: The unit X→Φ_S(X) is universally W^d because for prelisse families W^d=W^f, and W^f is preserved by all strict base changes.

statement: For prelisse X and Y, W^d-equivalence is equivalent to fibrewise W-equivalence; this remains true after base change.
repair: Compare each fibre map with its under-comma map through the two universal prelisse comparisons, and use two-out-of-three.

statement: To test preservation of base homotopy equivalences one can replace the family by its split comma fibration.
repair: The units before and after base change are W-maps; the projection maps form a commuting square, so two-out-of-three transfers the conclusion.

statement: The map of total categories represents p′_!f^*ξ→p_!ξ in Hot_W.
gap_or_error: The derivator adjunction and compatibility with the actual map of total categories are admitted, not reconstructed here.
repair: State both identifications explicitly; the formal Hom argument is valid once they are established.

statement: Adjunction and full faithfulness of f^* on locally constant coefficients make the comparison an isomorphism.
repair: The map on Hom(-,η) identifies with Hom(ξ,p^*η)→Hom(f^*ξ,f^*p^*η), a bijection. Yoneda proves invertibility of the specified comparison.
notes: This conclusion is in Hot_W; do not silently replace it by W-membership.

statement: Theorem 3: under W(1,2,3), the eight conditions a,a′,a1,a2,b1,b2,c1,c2 are equivalent.
repair: Combine Proposition 8 and its dual with the explicit contraction proof. The commentary gives the implication chain and keeps full relative W(2) visible.
notes: This theorem explicitly strengthens the weak standing definition used at the opening of section III.

statement: In Theorem 3, a (all maps between contractible bases) is equivalent to a′ (each fibre inclusion over a contractible base).
repair: a⇒a′ uses e→T. For a′⇒a, pick t in the nonempty contractible domain; the same fibre includes into both total categories, and two-out-of-three applies.

statement: The terminal-object and initial-object formulations are respectively equivalent to the two comma-transport and preproper/prelisse pseudofibration formulations.
repair: These are Proposition 8 and its dual. In b2 the comma arrow must be s1\X→s0\X, as already corrected in the edition.

statement: Either one-sided condition implies the other and the full contractible-base condition.
repair: Use the split replacement on the appropriate side and the finite contraction zigzag. This supplies the nontrivial bridge between the two triples of conditions.

statement: Theorem 3(d): pullback of a categorical homotopy equivalence of bases becomes an isomorphism in Hot_W.
repair: Apply the split replacement and the formal Hom/adjunction computation from ms49–50.
notes: Homotopy equivalence is a property of the underlying base functor; the functor also lies over S.

statement: With strong saturation, d gives an actual W-map and is equivalent to the eight other conditions.
repair: Strong saturation converts the localized isomorphism to W-membership; every map between nonempty categorically contractible categories is a categorical homotopy equivalence. Under full W(2), later strong saturation is automatic.

statement: Definition 4: W-fibration means the equivalent conditions a through c2 of the preceding theorem.
gap_or_error: The printed reference says Proposition 9, which has no eight-condition list.
repair: The intended reference is Theorem 3, ms51. Keep the printed reference and record the edition slip.

statement: Corollary 1: a W-proper or W-smooth map is a W-fibration iff it is a W-pseudofibration.
repair: Proper/smooth implies the relevant universal preproper/prelisse condition; apply Theorem 3(c1) or (c2).

statement: Corollary 2: a Cat-fibration is a W-fibration iff all u^* lie in W; dually for an opfibration and u_*.
repair: The fibre-comma comparisons for a Grothendieck fibration have adjoints, and comma transport corresponds to the chosen Cartesian transport up to these comparisons.
notes: The printed 'pout' is an edition typo, not an altered mathematical condition.

statement: Corollary 3: preproper plus prelisse, in particular perfect, implies W-fibration.
repair: The two universal comma comparisons imply both interval endpoint tests; Theorem 3 then applies.

statement: Proposition 10: a fibrewise W-map between W-fibrations over S is a W-map on total categories.
repair: Compare strict fibres with comma categories, apply full relative W(2), and use its dual when using under-commas.
notes: This is the direction from fibres to total; W(4b) is the separate converse.

statement: Footnote 59: Proposition 10 needs only both structural maps preproper or both prelisse.
repair: The two vertical arrows in each fibre-to-comma square and the fibre map are in W, hence so is the comma map. Relative W(2) yields the total map.

statement: The split-replacement proof of Proposition 10 follows from fibrewise units and Proposition 5.
gap_or_error: The fibrewise unit requires prelissity (already corrected in the edition); the cited result is precisely the corollary to Proposition 5.
repair: The replacements are smooth over S, and their induced comparison is fibrewise W. The corollary to Proposition 5 applies without requiring that comparison functor itself to be smooth.

statement: W(4a): a pullback of a W-map along any W-fibration belongs to W.
notes: The W-fibration notion is Definition 4/Theorem 3, not the earlier stronger definition. Stability under base change makes this the ultrafibration property.

statement: W(4a′): the same pullback assertion restricted to Wω-perfect maps.
repair: Wω is the minimum class for W(1,2 bis,3), hence W∞ by the later minimal weak-localizer theorem.

statement: W(4b): a W-map between W-fibrations over one base is in W on every fibre.
notes: This reverses Proposition 10 and is not obtained from it.

statement: W(4b′): restrict W(4b) to split Grothendieck fibrations and functors preserving the splittings.
notes: The structural families are still required to be W-fibrations; split alone is insufficient.

statement: W(4b″): restrict W(4b) to W-perfect structural maps.
notes: Perfect structural maps satisfy the W-fibration condition by Theorem 3.

statement: W(4c): a W-fibration which is a W-map has W-aspherical strict fibres.
notes: The codomain structural family in W(4b) is the identity family.

statement: W(4c′): a Wω-perfect functor which belongs to W has W-aspherical strict fibres.
notes: This is the weakest perfect-fibre test used in the earlier classification argument.

statement: The new W(4c′) is the earlier W(4b″), with the unnecessary W∞ qualification removed.
repair: Compare the contents, not the old lettering: fibres are W-aspherical, as already corrected at ms14.
These follow by restricting the tested class of maps, using perfect⇒W-fibration, or setting the second family equal to the identity.

statement: W(4a′)⇒W(4b) follows from the earlier proof of Proposition 4.
gap_or_error: Footnote 61 and the crossed arrow correctly identify the problem: that proof used a stronger fibration definition than Theorem 3.
repair: Do not reuse that proof unchanged. The weakest perfect test can instead be obtained by the earlier mapping-path argument, and the later classification yields the full conclusion.
notes: The implication's modern truth does not validate the cited historical proof.

statement: Does W(4c′) imply W(4c)?
repair: Yes, retrospectively: minimality plus the repaired nondegeneracy/iterated homotopy-fibre argument shows W=W∞ or all maps under W(1,2 bis,3) and c′. Both alternatives satisfy c.

statement: Does W(4c) imply W(4b)?
repair: Yes by the same classification, since c implies c′. The manuscript does not prove this implication here.

statement: Proposition 1: W(4b) should imply the pullback conclusion q∈bar W.
gap_or_error: The author qualifies the statement and admits compatibility identifications in its proof.
repair: Given the locally constant restriction theorem and the adjunction/total-category comparisons, the Hom computation proves that the specific q becomes invertible. It is a statement about W-fibrations and W-base maps, with conclusion in bar W.

statement: The weaker split test W(4b′) should suffice for the same conclusion.
repair: Apply b′ to Φ_B(E)→Φ_B(B) for a W∞-perfect W-map E→B. The units are homotopy equivalences and each fibre comparison yields W-asphericity of E_b. Thus b′ implies c′, and the later classification completes the conclusion.

statement: W(4b″), perhaps with W(6 bis), should likewise suffice.
repair: Apply b″ to a Wω-perfect W-map E→B and the identity of B: Wω-perfect implies W-perfect. This gives c′. The later classification makes the extra filtered-colimit hypothesis unnecessary.
notes: Footnote 62's conjectural W(6 bis) requirement is preserved historically.

statement: For strongly saturated W, W(4a),W(4a′),W(4b) are equivalent.
gap_or_error: Only b⇒a is developed here; the claimed earlier a′⇒b proof has changed hypotheses.
repair: The formal b⇒bar-a proof gives b⇒a under strong saturation. The full equivalence is retrospectively supplied by the weakest-test classification, without treating the disputed arrow as proved in the source.

statement: The equivalence should also include W(4b′) and W(4b″).
repair: Both restricted tests imply c′ as detailed above; c′ forces W∞ or all maps. This also resolves the conjectural extensions.

statement: For a W-fibration X→Y, strict pullback represents p^*ξ and ξ is locally constant.
repair: Use universal prelissity and the split replacement, exactly as at ms49. The two occurrences of S in the surrounding paragraph should be Y.
notes: The base-name slip is recorded separately; the subsequent corollary legitimately renames bases S′→S.

statement: The homology comparison is represented by the actual functor q:X′→X.
gap_or_error: The source explicitly says this compatibility is admitted.
repair: The adjunction comparison must be identified with the projection on the chosen total-category representatives; an abstract isomorphism of objects would not suffice.
references: Cisinski2009LocallyConstant (Proposition 1.10 for the formal comparison mechanism)

statement: Corollary: under W(4b), a W-equivalence of bases preserves homology with pulled-back locally constant coefficients.
gap_or_error: Depends on the cited earlier equivalence theorem for locally constant restriction and the admitted adjunction formalism.
repair: Full faithfulness on locally constant coefficients gives a bijection of Hom groups/sets into every constant coefficient. Yoneda proves the comparison is an isomorphism.
references: Cisinski2009LocallyConstant (Theorem 1.3 and Proposition 1.10, later ordinary-homotopy version)

statement: Under W(4b), restriction along a W-map is an equivalence on locally constant coefficients (citing VI, p204).
repair: Treat the earlier theorem as the substantive input; the present Hom computation needs only full faithfulness, not essential surjectivity.
notes: The proof does not derive this input from Proposition 10 or from an arbitrary weak localizer.

statement: Item 1: fibrewise W-smoothness between W-smooth structural families does not imply smoothness of the total functor.
repair: Worked counterexample: C has endomorphism monoid N, X=Y=C×[1]; h is identity on fibres and sends each crossing label n to n+1. The lift of crossing label 0 is empty, so h is not W∞-smooth.

statement: Item 1 positive part: a splitting-preserving map of split fibrations is W-smooth if it is W-smooth on every fibre.
repair: An arrow in the target factors through its chosen Cartesian lift; the total lift category is identified with the lift category for the appropriate fibre functor. Fibrewise asphericity proves smoothness.

statement: Dually, a strict Cartesian map of split opfibrations is W-proper if it is fibrewise W-proper.
repair: Dualize the preceding lift-category argument; the relevant preservation condition is preservation of the chosen opcartesian lifts.

statement: Item 2: a splitting-preserving, fibrewise perfect map need not be globally perfect, even with W-fibred structural families.
repair: Take Y=S and X=Φ_S(S) for the fork S. Every fibre functor to e is perfect, all structural transports between comma categories are weak equivalences, but the outgoing lift obstruction prevents properness.
notes: The example is valid for W∞ and, with the empty-asphericity qualification, for nontrivial relative W.

statement: Proposition 2: over the fork S=(0→a,0→b), Φ_S(Z) is proper iff Z is empty.
gap_or_error: For a W-relative interpretation the trivial localizer must be excluded; if all functors are in W, even empty lift categories are W-aspherical.
repair: If Z has a branch-labelled object, pull it formally back to 0 and test the other branch; its outgoing lift category is empty. If every object of nonempty Z lies above 0, any outgoing lift to a branch is empty. Ordinary properness, and nontrivial W-properness, therefore fail.
notes: The original bare 'propre' is retained. The earlier companion VI pp190–192 already contains the fork/support calculation.

statement: In the application of Proposition 2, every fibre functor Φ(Z)_s→e is W-perfect.
repair: Every functor from a category to e is both a Grothendieck fibration and an opfibration: only identity arrows must be lifted.

statement: If Z→S is a W-fibration, then Φ_S(Z)→S is also a W-fibration.
repair: Theorem 3 gives prelissity and W-comma transport for Z. Those comma transports are exactly the split replacement's transitions.

statement: A nonempty W-fibration Z over the fork therefore gives the announced counterexample to fibrewise perfect⇒perfect.
repair: Choose Z=S with identity structural map. All s\S have initial objects; Φ_S(S) is a W∞-fibration and is not proper by the explicit empty lifting category.

statement: Proposition 3: under W(4a), a strict Cartesian map of split fibrations with W-fibrant fibre maps is W-fibrant.
gap_or_error: The printed proposition omits the preceding paragraph's assumption that both structural families are W-fibrations. It is false for W∞, which satisfies W(4a).
repair: Counterexample: ∫(e←e)=[1] includes as one arm of ∫(e←{a,b})=fork. Each component between discrete categories is perfect. Pullback along the other arm has fibres e and empty. A fully proved sufficient repair in the development assumes W(4a,b), structural transitions in W, and each component both W-smooth and W-fibrant.
references: Rezk1998Sharp (Theorem 7.1 for a related coherent gluing theorem)
notes: The repair covers the preceding fibrewise-perfect setting; it does not assert that adding only the omitted structural hypothesis proves the entire literal formulation.

statement: Final remark: an unconditional fibrewise-gluing result was hoped to prove W(4c)⇒W(4b), but the attempted proof required W(4a).
gap_or_error: Using W(4a) to establish the gluing lemma cannot by itself prove W(4c)⇒W(4b) without a separate implication to W(4a); moreover the printed gluing lemma is false as stated.
repair: Record the abandoned argument as circular for the intended goal. The later classification resolves c⇒b independently; Rezk's gluing theorem explicitly requires homotopy-Cartesian naturality squares.
